test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the 2014 Rangarajan Committee regarding national poverty lines in India, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹872 living in the rural areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹2,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,272 living in the rural areas should be considered poor.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rangarajan Committee was set up in 2012 to review the existing poverty line in India and suggest a new method to measure poverty.
 
• According to the 2014 Rangarajan Committee, a person with a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,407 in urban areas should be considered poor.
 
• The committee's recommendations were based on a broader definition of poverty that included essential non-food requirements such as healthcare, education, and transportation.
 
• This new poverty line was considered to be more realistic as it better reflected the increased cost of living in both rural and urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rangarajan Committee**

 
 
• The Rangarajan Committee was chaired by C. Rangarajan, a former Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor.
 
• The committee was tasked with reviewing the existing poverty estimation methodology and recommending a new methodology to measure poverty in India.
 
• The committee proposed a poverty line based on the consumption expenditure required to meet basic needs, including food, education, health, housing, and transportation.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Line**
 
 
• The poverty line is the minimum level of income deemed adequate in a particular country. In India, it is calculated based on the per capita consumption expenditure required to meet basic needs.
 
• Historically, the poverty line in India was determined based on the cost of a minimum calorie intake, but this method was criticized for being too narrow and not reflecting the true cost of living.
 
 
 
• **Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE)**
 
 
• MPCE refers to the average monthly expenditure of an individual. It is used as a measure to determine the poverty line.
 
• The MPCE includes expenses on food, clothing, rent, transportation, healthcare, education, and other essential services.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Estimation in India**
 
 
• Poverty estimation in India has undergone several revisions, with different committees recommending different methodologies based on changing economic conditions and living standards.
 
• Notable committees include the Planning Commission, the Tendulkar Committee (2009), and the Rangarajan Committee (2014).
 
• Each committee has contributed to refining the definition and measurement of poverty to ensure more accurate and comprehensive estimates.
